Test Case: Christmas Town page loads without error
Pre-conditions: User is logged in; Christmas Town is active (December)
Steps: 1. Navigate to /christmas_town.php
Expected Result: Page loads with no 404 / 500 error; Christmas Town map is visible

Test Case: Page shows graceful message when event is closed
Pre-conditions: User is logged in; Christmas Town is NOT active (off-season)
Steps: 1. Navigate to /christmas_town.php
Expected Result: Event-ended or coming-soon message displayed; no PHP fatal error, no blank page

Test Case: Casino-banned user cannot deposit
Pre-conditions: User has a casino ban applied, Christmas Town is active
Steps: 1. Navigate to the Pot mini-game area. 2. Attempt to deposit an eligible item.
Expected Result: Ban message displayed; deposit blocked; no PHP error, no inventory change

Test Case: Pot mini-game area is visible on the map
Pre-conditions: User is logged in; Christmas Town is active
Steps: 1. Navigate to /christmas_town.php. 2. Explore the map to find the Pot trigger location.
Expected Result: Pot mini-game trigger is visible and interactable on the map

Test Case: Depositing 1 item reduces player inventory by exactly 1
Pre-conditions: User has at least 1 eligible item (Candy / Alcohol / Energy Drink); Christmas Town active; it is that item category's round
Steps: 1. Note the current count of the eligible item in your inventory. 2. Open the Pot mini-game. 3. Select that item and confirm deposit. 4. Check inventory again.
Expected Result: Item count in inventory is exactly 1 less than before deposit

Test Case: Depositing the last copy of an item removes it completely from inventory
Pre-conditions: User has exactly 1 copy of the eligible item; Christmas Town active
Steps: 1. Confirm you have exactly 1 of the target item. 2. Deposit it into the pot. 3. Check inventory.
Expected Result: The item no longer appears in inventory at all

Test Case: Pot user (ID 4545) does NOT gain the deposited item
Pre-conditions: Access to admin / armoury lookup for user ID 4545; Christmas Town active
Steps: 1. Before deposit: check armoury of user 4545 for the item count. 2. Deposit an eligible item. 3. Check armoury of user 4545 again.
Expected Result: Item count for user 4545 is unchanged — the item is removed (destroyed at deposit), NOT transferred to pot user

Test Case: yourItemsInPot counter increments after deposit
Pre-conditions: User is in the Pot mini-game; at least 1 eligible item available
Steps: 1. Note the "Your items in pot" counter on the UI. 2. Deposit one item. 3. Observe counter.
Expected Result: Counter increases by 1 (e.g. 0 → 1, or 1 → 2)

Test Case: itemsRemaining counter decrements after deposit
Pre-conditions: User is in the Pot mini-game; at least 1 eligible item available
Steps: 1. Note the "Items remaining" counter (max 3). 2. Deposit one item. 3. Observe counter.
Expected Result: Counter decreases by 1 (e.g. 3 → 2)

Test Case: Correct confirmation message shown after deposit
Pre-conditions: User is in the Pot mini-game; eligible item available
Steps: 1. Deposit an eligible item. 2. Read the response message.
Expected Result: Message contains "You add your [item name]"

Test Case: Deposited item appears on the pot game board
Pre-conditions: User is in the Pot mini-game; eligible item available
Steps: 1. Deposit an eligible item. 2. Look at the pot game board.
Expected Result: The item icon / entry appears on the board display

Test Case: Activity log records the deposit (log ID 8936)
Pre-conditions: User is in the Pot mini-game; eligible item available
Steps: 1. Deposit an eligible item. 2. Check the player's activity log.
Expected Result: An entry appears recording the deposit of the specific item ID

Test Case: Depositing a non-owned item is rejected
Pre-conditions: User is in the Pot mini-game
Steps: 1. Attempt to submit a deposit request with an itemID that you do not own (e.g. using a direct POST with an invalid ID). 2. Check inventory.
Expected Result: Error message: ""You do not own this item or this item has wrong type""; inventory unchanged

Test Case: Depositing an item of the wrong category is rejected
Pre-conditions: User has both Candy and Alcohol items; current round requires Candy
Steps: 1. Open the Pot mini-game when the required category is Candy. 2. Attempt to deposit an Alcohol item instead. 3. Check inventory.
Expected Result: Deposit rejected with category/type mismatch error; inventory unchanged for both items

Test Case: Player cannot deposit more than 3 items in one game
Pre-conditions: User has 3 items already in the pot (yourItemsInPot = 3), has a 4th eligible item
Steps: 1. Confirm yourItemsInPot = 3. 2. Attempt to deposit a 4th item. 3. Check inventory.
Expected Result: Deposit rejected: ""You can not push item in pot""; inventory unchanged; pot count stays at 3

Test Case: Item category rotates correctly between rounds
Pre-conditions: User plays across multiple completed games
Steps: 1. Complete a Candy round (game finishes). 2. Start depositing in the next round. 3. Note which category is required. 4. Repeat for a third round.
Expected Result: Category cycles: Candy → Alcohol → Energy Drink → Candy (rotating)

Test Case: Game-closed state prevents new deposits
Pre-conditions: Current game timestamp is in the future (cooldown period)
Steps: 1. Wait for or observe the "next game" timer. 2. Attempt to deposit while countdown is active.
Expected Result: Response: gameAvailable = false; nextGame > 0; no deposit accepted

Test Case: Winner receives all deposited items when the game ends
Pre-conditions: Multiple players have deposited items (or simulate with one player filling all 3 slots)
Steps: 1. Record all items currently in the pot (categories and quantities). 2. Make the winning deposit (the one that triggers the win chance). 3. Check the winner's inventory.
Expected Result: Winner's inventory increases by the total count of all pot items (from all depositors combined)

Test Case: Multiple copies of the same item_id are summed correctly
Pre-conditions: At least 2 deposits of the same item_id are in the pot (e.g. 2× Candy A from different players or two deposits by the same player in two separate games that land in the same pot)
Steps: 1. Ensure the pot contains 2× item_id 847 and 1× item_id 923 (example). 2. Trigger the win. 3. Check winner's inventory.
Expected Result: Winner receives 2 of item 847 and 1 of item 923 — array_count_values groups correctly

Test Case: Winner receives FRESH armoury_inventory entries (not original rows)
Pre-conditions: Access to armoury_inventory table; game is about to end
Steps: 1. Note the armoury_inventory IDs of items deposited into the pot. 2. Trigger the win. 3. Check the winner's newly received items.
Expected Result: The winner's items have NEW armoury_inventory row IDs — they are not the same rows that were deposited (fresh creation, not transfer)

Test Case: All depositors have already lost their items (removed at deposit time)
Pre-conditions: Multiple players have deposited items
Steps: 1. Player A deposits item — verify item removed from A immediately. 2. Game finishes; Player B is the winner. 3. Check Player A's inventory after the win.
Expected Result: Player A's inventory does not change further after the win — the item was already removed at step 1

Test Case: Winner who was also a depositor gets correct net result
Pre-conditions: Player deposits 1 item into a pot and also wins the pot (e.g. solo test or specific timing)
Steps: 1. Player deposits 1 Candy (inventory: Candy -1). 2. Player's deposit triggers the win. 3. Check inventory.
Expected Result: Deposited item is gone (removed at deposit time); all pot items (including the one just deposited) are re-created fresh and added to the player. Net: inventory = original - 1 + all pot items

Test Case: Congratulations" message shown to winner when game ends"
Pre-conditions: Game is triggerable via deposit
Steps: 1. Make the winning deposit. 2. Read the response message.
Expected Result: Message contains "Congratulations, you won N item(s)"

Test Case: Pot board resets and new countdown timer shown after win
Pre-conditions: Game ends due to a winning deposit
Steps: 1. Observe the pot board before the win. 2. Trigger the win. 3. Observe the pot board after.
Expected Result: Board clears; new game timer/countdown (nextGame) is visible and > 0

Test Case: Activity log records reward for the winner (log ID 8938)
Pre-conditions: Game ends; winner is logged in
Steps: 1. Win the pot mini-game. 2. Check the winner's activity log.
Expected Result: An entry appears with the reward details including gameType 'Pot' and the item quantities received

Test Case: Inventory and MongoDB are consistent: no orphaned pot entries
Pre-conditions: Ability to inspect MongoDB game progress and armoury_inventory
Steps: 1. Deposit an item (removes from inventory + pushes to MongoDB). 2. Inspect MongoDB game document. 3. Inspect armoury_inventory for that item.
Expected Result: Item removed from armoury_inventory AND recorded in MongoDB game document — both changes either both committed or both rolled back

Test Case: Partial reward failure leaves no items lost or duplicated
Pre-conditions: Ability to simulate a mid-reward failure (dev environment)
Steps: 1. Set up a full pot (3 deposits across multiple item types). 2. Inject a failure during addSeveralItemsToArmoury (e.g. after first item type is added). 3. Observe the outcome.
Expected Result: If transaction rolls back: winner receives 0 items; all quantities accounted for. If it commits: all item types granted.

Test Case: Redis lock prevents concurrent double-spend on the same item
Pre-conditions: Two sessions belonging to the same user (or two users with the same eligible item)
Steps: 1. Open two browser tabs both on the Pot mini-game. 2. Send a deposit request simultaneously from both tabs for the same item. 3. Check inventory.
Expected Result: Exactly 1 deposit succeeds; inventory decremented by exactly 1; the second request is rejected with a lock/concurrency message

Test Case: itemsArmouryClass no longer exposes transferSeveralItemToNewUser
Pre-conditions: Dev / code review
Steps: 1. Search the codebase for any call to transferSeveralItemToNewUser. 2. Confirm none exist outside of removed code.
Expected Result: No remaining callers; method removed cleanly. Any call attempt would result in "method not found" — verify no other feature accidentally used this method.

Test Case: Trades / bazaar / item market still work normally after removal of transferSeveralItemToNewUser
Pre-conditions: Trading is possible (user has tradeable items, a trade partner available)
Steps: 1. Initiate a trade and add items. 2. Complete the trade. 3. Check both players' inventories.
Expected Result: Items transferred correctly in trade; no errors in server log referencing removed methods

Test Case: Faction armoury donations still work after the removal
Pre-conditions: User is in a faction with donate permission
Steps: 1. Go to Faction Controls → Armoury. 2. Donate an item to the faction armoury. 3. Check faction armoury and player inventory.
Expected Result: Item moved to faction armoury; player inventory decremented; no errors

Test Case: getArmouryIDsForUpdate is no longer called during any pot game flow
Pre-conditions: Dev / server log monitoring
Steps: 1. Play through a full pot mini-game (deposit + win). 2. Check server logs for any reference to getArmouryIDsForUpdate.
Expected Result: No log entries or errors mentioning getArmouryIDsForUpdate

Test Case: MongoDB game log dbItems field has new format after a win
Pre-conditions: Access to MongoDB logs; game is winnable
Steps: 1. Trigger a win. 2. Inspect the MongoDB log document for the game reward entry. 3. Look at the dbItems field.
Expected Result: dbItems contains {item_id: qty} map (e.g. {847: 3, 923: 1}) — NOT an array of armoury row objects

Test Case: composedReward in the log still contains correct armouryID values
Pre-conditions: Access to MongoDB logs; game is winnable
Steps: 1. Trigger a win. 2. Inspect the MongoDB log document's reward.composedReward array. 3. Check each entry's armouryID field.
Expected Result: Each entry has a valid armouryID populated from the $items array; no null/missing armouryID values

Test Case: handlePotMiniGameReward activity log (8938) counts items correctly
Pre-conditions: Access to activity log; game is winnable
Steps: 1. Win a pot game containing 3× item A and 2× item B. 2. Check activity log entry 8938 for the winner.
Expected Result: Log entry shows {itemA_id: 3; itemB_id: 2} — counts match exactly what was in the pot

Test Case: Empty pot (0 items) game state does not crash
Pre-conditions: Christmas Town active; pot is currently empty (just after a win / new game)
Steps: 1. Open the Pot mini-game immediately after a game ends (pot is empty). 2. Check the state response.
Expected Result: Game state returns cleanly: yourItemsInPot = 0; itemsRemaining = 3; no PHP error

Test Case: Single depositor wins all items they put in
Pre-conditions: Only one player has deposited into the pot; that player's deposit triggers the win chance
Steps: 1. Player deposits 3 items (filling the pot). 2. The winning deposit triggers a win. 3. Check player's inventory.
Expected Result: Player's 3 deposited items are gone (removed at deposit). 3 fresh items are created and awarded back to the same player.

Test Case: Energy Drink round works the same as Candy and Alcohol rounds
Pre-conditions: Current round requires Energy Drink items
Steps: 1. Confirm current category is "Energy Drink". 2. Attempt to deposit an Alcohol item (wrong type). 3. Deposit a valid Energy Drink item instead.
Expected Result: Step 2 rejected; Step 3 succeeds with correct inventory change and confirmation message

Test Case: Game board shows correct item count across all depositors
Pre-conditions: Multiple players have deposited different quantities
Steps: 1. Player A deposits 2 items; Player B deposits 1 item. 2. View the pot board.
